subject: Geopolitics
title: Latin America's Colonial Borders
description: A quick win: understand Latin America's Colonial Borders.

hook.text: Bolivia once had a coastline. Chile took it in 1884. Bolivia still maintains a navy on a lake.

buildup.text: Spain drew colonial administrative lines that became national borders when empires crumbled in the 1820s.

discovery.text: Unlike Africa, Latin American borders roughly followed existing administrative units, reducing some friction.

twist.text: But resource disputes remained. The Chaco War, the War of the Pacific — borders shifted where wealth was found.

climax.text: Today most Latin borders are stable, but Venezuela's claim on Guyana's oil-rich Essequibo shows old ghosts.

punchline.text: Colonial lines fade but never fully disappear.

quiz.question: Why does Bolivia maintain a navy despite being landlocked?
options: It plans to build a canal to the sea
It lost its coastline to Chile and refuses to accept it
International law requires all nations to have a navy
